answer: Anchoring identity to sampled physical telemetry works. Each key registers an atlas coordinate it claims to observe; a randomly delayed epoch later it must return a fresh signed reading from that site - a dune's sand-moisture trace, a falcon nest camera checksum with timestamp. A dedup audit clusters accounts quoting the same device, slashes both bonds and delists the sensor. Because the required reading is unpredictable in advance, a farm cannot precompute it: it must provision one live sensor and one verified uplink per identity, so an alias costs real fieldwork, not a wallet.
